# Chilled Water Plant Sequence of Operations
**Hospital Central Plant – CH-1/2/3, CHWP-1/2/3, CWP-1/2/3, CT-1/2/3**

## 1. General

1.1 **Plant description.** Three 800-ton water-cooled VFD centrifugal chillers (CH-1/2/3) in a variable primary flow (VPF) arrangement. Each chiller is paired with a headered VFD primary pump (CHWP-1/2/3) and a headered condenser pump (CWP-1/2/3), and is served by cooling towers CT-1/2/3 with VFD fans. Chiller minimum flow is 960 gpm and design flow is 1600 gpm.

1.2 **Capacity and redundancy.** Plant capacity is N+1: any two chillers must be able to serve the design load with the third as standby. The BAS shall never intentionally reduce available capacity below N+1 unless alarmed and acknowledged by an operator.

1.3 **Critical load.** Continuity of cooling to the surgery suites takes priority over efficiency. Where a requirement here conflicts with efficiency, the reliability requirement governs.

1.4 **Modes.** Each chiller, pump, and tower cell has a HAND-OFF-AUTO (HOA) selection. The sequence applies to equipment in AUTO. Plant enable is by operator command or schedule, with an outdoor-air lockout adjustable (initial 40°F) that is overridden to allow operation whenever any critical zone calls for cooling.

1.5 **Lead/lag/standby.** The operator shall designate lead, lag, and standby chillers. The BAS shall rotate the lead automatically on a runtime basis (adjustable, initial weekly) and on a failure of the lead. Each chiller shall be paired with its pump, condenser pump, and isolation valves as a unit, and a failure of any element shall make the entire unit unavailable.

## 2. Points (Summary)

| Tag | Description |
|---|---|
| DPT-710 | Remote differential pressure at critical AHU, setpoint 12 psid (adjustable) |
| FIT-702 | Common primary loop flow meter |
| FCV-701 | Bypass valve for minimum flow |
| CHWST / CHWRT | Plant supply and return temperatures |
| Per chiller | Status, alarm, % RLA, evaporator and condenser entering/leaving temperatures, isolation valve position/status |
| Coil valve positions | Air handler cooling coil valve positions, used for CHWST reset |

Redundant DPT-710 sensors, or a second remote sensor at another critical AHU, are recommended. See 8.2.

## 3. Plant Enable and Chiller Start Sequence

3.1 On plant enable, the BAS starts the lead chiller's sequence in this order:

1. Open the chiller's chilled water isolation valve and condenser water isolation valve (prove open by end switch).
2. Start the condenser pump CWP and prove flow (flow switch or differential pressure).
3. Start the primary pump CHWP and prove flow. If FIT-702 is used for proving, the flow must be at or above the chiller minimum.
4. Enable the tower sequence (Section 6).
5. After flow is proven and condenser water temperature is above the chiller manufacturer's minimum, enable the chiller start.
6. Chiller start is permissive on the chiller's own safeties, and the BAS shall monitor chiller status feedback. If status is not proven within an adjustable time (initial 5 min), the BAS shall alarm, lock out that unit, and start the next available unit in the sequence.

3.2 Stopping is the reverse: the chiller is commanded off, then the pump and valves run on for an adjustable delay (initial 5 min) before they are shut down, so that residual heat is rejected.

## 4. Chiller Staging

4.1 **Staging up.** The BAS shall start the next chiller when any of the following holds for an adjustable time (initial 10 min):

- Running chillers' average load exceeds 90% (adj.) of full-load capacity, **or**
- The CHWST exceeds setpoint by 1.5°F (adj.) with running chillers at their current limit or at maximum capacity, **or**
- Plant load, calculated from FIT-702 and the CHWRT–CHWST difference, exceeds 90% (adj.) of the capacity of the running chillers.

Immediate staging (no time delay) occurs on a chiller trip or failure to prove, or when the CHWST exceeds setpoint by 3°F (adj.).

4.2 **Staging down.** The BAS shall stop the last-started chiller when the calculated plant load is below 75% (adj.) of the capacity of the remaining chillers, and the remaining chillers' projected load is below 85%, for an adjustable time (initial 15 min). The BAS shall not stage down if it would leave the plant unable to carry the load or when a critical-load alarm is active. A minimum run time (initial 20 min) and a minimum off time (initial 10 min) apply.

4.3 **Transition.** On starting a chiller, its CHWP is started and its isolation valve opened before the chiller starts, so the flow through the running chillers is not disrupted. Chiller isolation valves shall stroke slowly (per actuator speed) to avoid flow upsets. On a stop, the load is shed (ramped via demand limit) before the isolation valve is closed.

4.4 **Load-sharing.** The running chillers share load equally (equal leaving-water setpoint). Chiller VFDs are controlled by the chiller's onboard controls. The BAS does not override them except by demand limit and setpoint.

## 5. Primary Chilled Water Pump and Bypass Control

5.1 **Pump speed.** The running primary pumps shall operate at a common speed, modulated by a PID loop to maintain DPT-710 at its setpoint (12 psid, adjustable). The loop output is limited at the minimum speed (adj.) and at maximum speed.

5.2 **Pump staging.** The number of pumps running equals the number of chillers running (one pump per chiller). Because the pumps are headered, the BAS shall not run a pump without its associated chiller, except during the run-on period and when a standby pump is commanded due to a failure (5.5).

5.3 **Minimum flow bypass.** FCV-701 shall be closed in normal operation. Its PID loop modulates the valve open to maintain FIT-702 at or above the total minimum flow of the running chillers (960 gpm × number of chillers running, plus an adjustable margin, initial 5%). The valve shall close again when flow is above the minimum by an adjustable deadband. The bypass loop shall be tuned so that it takes priority over the DPT-710 loop at low loads, and the pump speed shall not be reduced to a point that results in a flow below the minimum.

5.4 **Maximum flow.** If the flow through any chiller would exceed the design (1600 gpm) or manufacturer's maximum, the BAS shall limit pump speed and alarm.

5.5 **Pump failure.** On failure of a running CHWP (no flow, VFD fault), the BAS shall alarm and start the standby chiller/pump unit. Where the chiller is otherwise healthy and the standby is not available, the BAS shall allow the failed pump's chiller to be served by another pump through the header, if the piping arrangement permits, and shall confirm this arrangement with the design engineer. Otherwise the associated chiller shall be shut down.

5.6 **Flow-loss protection.** On loss of flow at a running chiller (flow switch or FIT-702 below minimum for an adjustable time, initial 30 s, with the bypass fully open), the chiller shall be stopped by the BAS and the standby unit started.

## 6. Condenser Water and Cooling Towers

6.1 **Condenser pumps.** CWP-n runs with CH-n. CWP failure is handled as in 5.5.

6.2 **Tower staging.** The number of tower cells enabled follows the number of running chillers (adjustable), with additional cells added if the condenser water supply temperature exceeds setpoint by an adjustable amount. Tower isolation valves, if provided, open before the cell is enabled.

6.3 **Fan control.** The tower fans of all enabled cells operate at the same speed. A PID loop modulates fan speed to maintain the condenser water supply temperature (CWST) at setpoint. The setpoint is reset by the outdoor air wet-bulb: setpoint = wet-bulb + approach (adj., initial 7°F), limited to a minimum (the chiller manufacturer's minimum entering condenser water temperature, initial 65°F, adj.) and a maximum (initial 85°F, adj.).

6.4 **Freeze protection.** If the basin temperature drops below 40°F (adj.), the BAS shall energize the basin heaters and shall alarm. Operation in cold weather (bypass valves, fan reversal, and so on) is by the tower manufacturer's requirements and shall be defined in the submittal.

6.5 **Free cooling.** Not included in this scope. The sequence shall be extended if a waterside economizer is added.

## 7. Chilled Water Supply Temperature Reset

7.1 The default CHWST setpoint is 42°F. It may be reset upward to a maximum of 46°F based on the cooling coil valve positions of the air handlers, using trim-and-respond logic:

- Request: any air handler coil valve at more than 95% open (adj.) for 5 min generates a request.
- Evaluation every 5 min (adj.): with zero requests (or fewer than the ignored number, initial 2), raise the setpoint by 0.5°F. With more than the ignored requests, lower the setpoint by 1°F. Limits are 42°F to 46°F.

7.2 Reset is disabled, and the setpoint returns to 42°F, when any of the following applies: a critical-zone air handler (surgery suites) has a coil valve at over 90% open, any critical zone alarm is active (temperature or humidity), plant capacity is below N+1, or DPT-710 is in fault.

7.3 The reset shall not cause the chillers to cycle, and the setpoint changes must be rate limited (maximum 1°F per 10 min on the way up).

## 8. Reliability and Failure Modes (Hospital Critical Requirements)

8.1 **N+1.** The BAS shall continuously calculate the available capacity (healthy, available units in AUTO) and alarm at high priority if available capacity falls below N+1. If the number of available chillers is less than three, the BAS shall also inhibit the CHWST reset (7.2) and the stage-down of the standby (4.2).

8.2 **Sensor failure.** If DPT-710 fails (out of range or a bad signal), the pumps shall go to a fixed speed (adj.) that gives the design differential pressure at the current load, as determined during commissioning. The BAS shall alarm. If a second remote DPT is provided, the control shall use the lower of the valid signals (or the sensor with the lowest margin to its setpoint, as defined by the engineer). If FIT-702 fails, the BAS shall open FCV-701 to a position that guarantees minimum flow (set during commissioning), and alarm.

8.3 **Standby start on failure.** On a trip or fault on any running chiller, pump, or condenser pump, the BAS shall automatically start the standby unit as per 4.1 (immediate) and alarm. The standby start-up shall be sequenced to avoid a simultaneous inrush by staggering starts (adjustable delay).

8.4 **Power failure and restart.** After a power loss, equipment restarts automatically in a staggered order, with the following priority: primary pumps and condenser pumps, then towers, then chillers (one at a time, with an adjustable delay, initial 2 min). The BAS shall not command any equipment that is on emergency power in excess of the generator's capacity. The electrical engineer shall define the equipment on the emergency system, and the BAS shall use a generator-running or ATS status input to limit the number of chillers allowed (adjustable) while on generator.

8.5 **BAS and communication failure.** On loss of communication between the BAS controllers and the plant, each chiller shall continue to run on its own onboard controls. The pump VFDs shall go to a fixed speed (adj.), FCV-701 shall hold the last position or go to a failsafe position (the valve fails open per its actuator), and the towers shall run at the last speed or a fixed speed. The plant shall not shut down because of a loss of communication.

8.6 **Manual override.** Hand operation at the equipment and at the BAS workstation shall be possible, and the BAS shall alarm when any equipment is in HAND.

8.7 **Chilled water system pressure.** Low-pressure and high-pressure alarms are provided on the loop. The expansion tank or make-up arrangement is not in the BAS scope unless noted.

## 9. Alarms (Minimum)

| Priority | Alarm |
|---|---|
| Critical | Available capacity below N+1; loss of flow at a running chiller; CHWST high (setpoint +3°F, 10 min); DPT-710 failure; chiller trip; all-chillers-off with plant enabled |
| High | Pump or condenser pump failure; failure to prove status; FCV-701 not achieving minimum flow; high condenser water temperature; chiller low-temperature or other safeties |
| Medium | Equipment in HAND; excessive runtime differences; tower basin low temperature; FIT-702 failure |
| Low | Maintenance runtime thresholds; reset limits reached |

Critical alarms are annunciated to the facilities operations staff and the hospital's central alarm panel as defined by the owner.

## 10. Trending, Graphics, and Commissioning

10.1 **Trends.** Trend all points at 1-minute (analog) or change-of-state (binary) intervals for 30 days at a minimum, including the setpoints, DPT-710, FIT-702, FCV-701 position, pump speeds, chiller loads, CHWST/CHWRT, CWST, tower fan speeds, the computed plant load (tons), and the plant kW/ton.

10.2 **Graphics.** Provide a plant overview showing the status of all the equipment, flows, temperatures, available capacity vs. N+1, and the active reset state.

10.3 **Functional testing.** Commissioning shall include a witnessed test of the following: each chiller's start and stop sequences; stage-up and stage-down; simulated loss of each chiller, pump, and condenser pump under load; DPT-710 and FIT-702 failure; communication loss; a power failure and generator transfer; and the bypass valve performance at minimum flow. Tuning constants shall be recorded in the commissioning report.

## 11. Items for Design Engineer Confirmation

1. The headered pump arrangement. With one pump per chiller but a common header, confirm whether a standby pump can serve any chiller, and whether a dedicated standby pump or a fourth pump should be provided so that the loss of a pump does not reduce the chiller capacity (relevant to N+1).
2. Bypass valve sizing, so FCV-701 can pass the minimum flow of the largest running configuration and its fail position.
3. The chillers on emergency power, and generator capacity (8.4).
4. A second remote DPT or redundant sensors at a different critical AHU.
5. Chiller minimum condenser water temperature and the maximum rate of load change, from the manufacturer.
6. All values marked "adj." and "initial" are starting values that are to be tuned in commissioning.
